hints: Notice this solid has two parts to think about, the nitrate part and the water of crystallisation part.
Recall how a Group 2 nitrate like $\text{Mg(NO}_3)_2$ breaks down on strong heating, what solid and what gases form?
Think about what gentle heat does first to the $6\text{H}_2\text{O}$, and where that vapour goes in a cool test-tube.
walkthrough:
**Separate gentle heating from strong heating**

Gentle heat drives off water of crystallisation first before the nitrate itself decomposes. This is a physical dehydration step.

$$\text{Mg(NO}_3)_2.6\text{H}_2\text{O(s)} \rightarrow \text{Mg(NO}_3)_2\text{(s)} + 6\text{H}_2\text{O(l/g)}$$

**Explain statement 3**

The water vapour rises and condenses on the cooler upper walls of the test-tube. That is why you see colourless droplets of liquid.

So statement 3 is correct.

**Decompose the anhydrous magnesium nitrate**

On strong heating, magnesium nitrate undergoes thermal decomposition like all Group 2 nitrates except barium. It forms a basic oxide, nitrogen dioxide and oxygen.

$$2\text{Mg(NO}_3)_2\text{(s)} \rightarrow 2\text{MgO(s)} + 4\text{NO}_2\text{(g)} + \text{O}_2\text{(g)}$$

**Explain statements 1 and 2**

$\text{MgO}$ is a Group 2 oxide, so it is basic and remains as a white solid residue. $\text{NO}_2$ is the familiar brown, pungent gas.

So statements 1 and 2 are both correct, and 1, 2 and 3 together are correct.

options.A: Correct, because all three statements are true. Gentle heat releases water of crystallisation which condenses, and strong heat decomposes $\text{Mg(NO}_3)_2$ to basic $\text{MgO}$ plus brown $\text{NO}_2$ and $\text{O}_2$.
options.B: Incorrect, because it leaves out statement 3. Students choose this if they focus only on nitrate decomposition and forget that hydrated salts release water on gentle warming to give condensation.
options.C: Incorrect, because it leaves out statement 1. Students choose this if they remember the brown $\text{NO}_2$ gas and the water droplets but doubt that $\text{MgO}$ is left as a basic residue.
options.D: Incorrect, because it includes only statement 1. Students choose this if they confuse magnesium nitrate with a Group 1 nitrate that gives a nitrite, or think no brown gas or water is seen.
